cards.title: Distinction Between Prediction Uncertainty and Population Variability
cards.claim: In human dose prediction, 'uncertainty' refers to limited knowledge of the system (e.g., scaling error) and decreases as information accumulates, whereas 'variability' is an inherent property of the system (e.g., inter-individual differences) that does not decrease with larger sample sizes. Conflating these leads to misinterpretation of prediction intervals.
conditions: Applicable to all prospective human PK/PD simulations.
Requires explicit separation of scaling methodology uncertainty from target population biological variability.
required_inputs: Point estimates for PK parameters (CL, Vss).
Defined uncertainty distributions for scaling parameters.
Defined variability distributions for population parameters.
limitations: PD uncertainty is harder to generalize than PK uncertainty and varies by biological system.
Uncertainty in PD effect depends on the specific preclinical model and study design.
cards.downstream_use: Guides the construction of Monte Carlo simulation inputs and the interpretation of prediction intervals.

note: Method/reference scope retained; source identity is available in original evidence.
